overview: This bill, the YALI Act of 2026, puts into law the Young African Leaders Initiative, a State Department program started in 2010 to build ties with emerging leaders in sub-Saharan Africa. The program would offer training, networking, and business and technical support in areas such as entrepreneurship, good governance, public administration, and human rights. It would continue the Mandela Washington Fellowship, which brings Africans aged 25 to 35 to the United States for a six-week leadership program at an American college and a yearly summit, and would allow exchanges between Americans and program alumni. The State Department would have to give Congress an implementation plan with goals within 180 days and publish yearly progress reports, and the program would end after five years unless renewed. As of February 10, 2026, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say making the program permanent in law, with clear goals and reporting, strengthens U.S. relationships with Africa's next generation of business and government leaders.
against: Critics say the bill commits the government to an ongoing exchange program without setting its funding level, and that the long-term payoff of leadership exchanges can be hard to measure.
